I’m not going to say I was wrong just because the class agrees — but I can see why your professor may have raised the “wartime exception.” The key distinction is **current law vs. older/historical law**.

**Short answer for current Swiss law:**  
**No. The death penalty is not legal anywhere in Switzerland, including in wartime.**

The controlling point is **Art. 10 para. 1 of the Swiss Federal Constitution** (in force since 1 January 2000):

> “Every person has the right to life. **The death penalty is prohibited.**”

That provision is **absolute** — it does **not** contain a wartime carve-out.

## How the “military criminal code / wartime exception” fits in

The “wartime exception” your professor may be referring to is likely from an **older version** of Swiss law or an older treaty framework:

- Switzerland abolished the death penalty for ordinary **peacetime** crimes in **1996**.
- A remaining **wartime/military** death-penalty provision in the Military Criminal Code existed historically; the final removal/overriding of that remaining military wartime exception is commonly dated to **2002**.
- In any event, since the 1999 Federal Constitution, **Art. 10 para. 1 BV** absolutely prohibits the death penalty, so any conflicting statutory provision cannot be a valid current legal basis for execution.

So if your course materials say “there is still a wartime exception in the military criminal code,” they are either:

1. using an **outdated text** of the Military Criminal Code;  
2. referring to the old **ECHR Protocol 6** framework, which allowed a possible wartime exception; or  
3. discussing the **historical rule**, not current enforceable Swiss law.

## What to say on the exam

If the question is: **“Is the death penalty legal in Switzerland today?”**  
Answer: **No. Art. 10 para. 1 BV prohibits it absolutely, with no wartime exception.**

If the professor’s question is more like: **“Was there ever a wartime exception in the Military Criminal Code?”**  
Then the answer is: **Yes, historically there was; but it is no longer a current legal basis under Swiss law.**

If your professor insists it is “still” there, I would be safe in asking: **“For which version/date of the Military Criminal Code, and how is that reconciled with Art. 10 para. 1 BV?”** A valid current Swiss legal rule cannot authorize a death penalty that the Constitution expressly prohibits.
